item.title: Thousands are still without power in Gary, Ind., nearly two weeks after storms
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Kaitlin Washburn, reporter with the Chicago Sun-Times, about the ongoing power outages in northwest Indiana and how they're affecting residents' lives.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Kaitlin Washburn, reporter with the Chicago Sun-Times, about the ongoing power outages in northwest Indiana and how they're affecting residents' lives.

item.title: This scientist uses light to perform smarter, cleaner chemistry
item.description: To create the molecules we need to help us grow food or make fuel, we rely on chemical reactions — and lots of energy. One scientist may have a "brighter" approach, controlling chemistry with light.

item.title: Lab-grown organoids are living longer — offering new insight into the human brain
item.description: A study in the journal Nature sets a new record for the lifespan of lab-grown cells called organoids. These clusters of human cells in petri dishes are used as models of the human brain.
item.content:encoded: A study in the journal Nature sets a new record for the lifespan of lab-grown cells called organoids. These clusters of human cells in petri dishes are used as models of the human brain.

item.title: A look at the future of brain research funding, from a kids' camp for TBI survivors
item.description: A Pennsylvania summer camp helps children who have survived brain injuries. But the future of federal funding for brain injury research, and grants to states to help such patients, is in limbo.

item.title: The latest twists and turns in the proposed Paramount and Warner Bros. merger
item.description: The proposed merger between Hollywood heavyweights Paramount and Warner Bros. continues to inch along. Many in the film industry hope to block the deal — but now some are calling for a settlement.

item.title: Bad Bunny wraps tour, brings joy home to Puerto Rico
item.description: After a global tour, Puerto Rican superstar Bad Bunny returned home for two final concerts this weekend. He urged residents to continue fighting for improvements on the island.

item.title: Move over beer. In Rwanda, a bar might pour you a glass of milk
item.description: Milk is a popular drink in Rwanda, associated with economic prosperity. But as the country sees a rise in obesity and cholesterol, the health ministry aims to curb people's habit of drinking it daily.

item.title: DHS conducted far-reaching surveillance amid Minnesota ICE surge, court documents show
item.description: DHS allegedly conducted a huge surveillance operation during the ICE surge in Minnesota last winter, sweeping up activists, labor unions and others.

item.title: U.S. Treasury launches 'economic D-Day' against Iran as war drags on
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled new economic sanctions package against Iran. It includes measures to impose sanctions on anyone that deals with the Islamic regime in Tehran.

item.title: Novelist Jade Chang on the point of our existence
item.description: To help us hang on to summer vibes, we invited author Jade Chang to share a couple of the books she's reading and to talk about he own novel, What a Time to be Alive.
